1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh — the default claim
3	# coordinator (ADR-005): one shared issue label, zbuild:claimed, means "a run is
4	# working on this issue". Who holds it is in that run's run-status comment.
5	# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; do not add set -euo pipefail.
6	
7	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_CLAIM_GH_LABELS_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
8	_ZBUILD_CLAIM_GH_LABELS_LOADED=1
9	
10	_CCGL_LABEL="zbuild:claimed"
11	_CCGL_DIR="${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}"
12	
13	# Backends: `gh` (the default) talks to GitHub; `local-fs` keeps the labels in
14	# ZBUILD_CLAIM_STORE/<issue>/labels.txt, flock-serialised, for tests.
15	_ccgl_flock_timeout_sec() { echo "${ZBUILD_CLAIM_FLOCK_TIMEOUT_SEC:-5}"; }
16	
17	_ccgl_lf_labels_file() {
18	    local issue="$1"
19	    local store="${ZBUILD_CLAIM_STORE:?ZBUILD_CLAIM_STORE must be set for local-fs backend}"
20	    mkdir -p "$store/$issue"
21	    echo "$store/$issue/labels.txt"
22	}
23	
24	# Every gh call runs under the run-status comment's watchdog (rsc_gh,
25	# ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_GH_TIMEOUT): a hung gh in the exit path could otherwise
26	# only be KILLed, and would leave the label behind.
27	_ccgl_gh_lib() {
28	    declare -F rsc_gh >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
29	    # shellcheck source=../../../scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh
30	    source "${_ZBUILD_ROOT:-$_CCGL_DIR/../../..}/scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh"
31	}
32	_CCGL_OUT=""
33	_ccgl_gh() {
34	    _ccgl_gh_lib || return 1
35	    local out rc=0
36	    out="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ccgl-gh.XXXXXX")" || return 1
37	    rsc_gh "${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}" "$out" "$@" || rc=$?
38	    _CCGL_OUT="$(cat "$out" 2>/dev/null)"
39	    rm -f "$out"
40	    return "$rc"
41	}
42	
43	# The repository every label call and the holder reader name: one slug, the
44	# same for both (GITHUB_REPOSITORY in CI, else the origin's). rc 1 when none.
45	_CCGL_SLUG=""
46	_ccgl_slug() {
47	    [[ -n "$_CCGL_SLUG" ]] && return 0
48	    _ccgl_gh_lib || return 1
49	    _CCGL_SLUG="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}"
50	    [[ -n "$_CCGL_SLUG" ]] || _CCGL_SLUG="$(zbuild_repo_slug 2>/dev/null || true)"
51	    [[ -n "$_CCGL_SLUG" ]]
52	}
53	
54	# Labels on an issue, one a line, into _CCGL_OUT. rc 1 on a backend error.
55	_ccgl_read_labels() {
56	    local issue="$1"
57	    case "${ZBUILD_CLAIM_BACKEND:-gh}" in
58	        gh) _ccgl_slug && _ccgl_gh issue view "$issue" --json labels --jq '.labels[].name' --repo "$_CCGL_SLUG" ;;
59	        local-fs)
60	            local f; f="$(_ccgl_lf_labels_file "$issue")"
61	            _CCGL_OUT=""
62	            [[ -f "$f" ]] && _CCGL_OUT="$(cat "$f")"
63	            return 0 ;;
64	        *) return 1 ;;
65	    esac
66	}
67	
68	# rc 0 when <label> is on <issue> now (one read).
69	_ccgl_label_on() {
70	    local line
71	    _ccgl_read_labels "$1" || return 1
72	    while IFS= read -r line; do [[ "$line" == "$2" ]] && return 0; done <<< "$_CCGL_OUT"
73	    return 1
74	}
75	
76	# Add the label. rc 0 added, 2 already there (local-fs: checked inside the lock),
77	# 1 backend error. A repository that does not define the label yet gets it once.
78	_ccgl_add_label() {
79	    local issue="$1" label="$2"
80	    case "${ZBUILD_CLAIM_BACKEND:-gh}" in
81	        gh)
82	            _ccgl_slug || return 1
83	            _ccgl_gh issue edit "$issue" --add-label "$label" --repo "$_CCGL_SLUG" && return 0
84	            if [[ "$_RSC_GH_ERR" == *"not found"* ]]; then
85	                _ccgl_gh label create "$label" --force --color "5319e7" \
86	                    --description "a zbuild run is working on this issue" --repo "$_CCGL_SLUG" || return 1
87	                _ccgl_gh issue edit "$issue" --add-label "$label" --repo "$_CCGL_SLUG" && return 0
88	            fi
89	            # The add may have reached GitHub with its answer lost (a timeout, a
90	            # dropped reply). The issue was clear when read, so a label there now
91	            # is this run's: say so, or nothing would ever release it.
92	            _ccgl_label_on "$issue" "$label"
93	            ;;
94	        local-fs)
95	            local f; f="$(_ccgl_lf_labels_file "$issue")"
96	            local timeout; timeout="$(_ccgl_flock_timeout_sec)"
97	            (
98	                exec 9>"${f}.lock"
99	                flock -w "$timeout" 9 || exit 1
100	                touch "$f"
101	                grep -Fxq "$label" "$f" && exit 2
102	                echo "$label" >> "$f"
103	                exit 0
104	            )
105	            ;;
106	        *) return 1 ;;
107	    esac
108	}
109	
110	_ccgl_remove_label() {
111	    local issue="$1" label="$2"
112	    case "${ZBUILD_CLAIM_BACKEND:-gh}" in
113	        gh) _ccgl_slug && _ccgl_gh issue edit "$issue" --remove-label "$label" --repo "$_CCGL_SLUG" ;;
114	        local-fs)
115	            local f; f="$(_ccgl_lf_labels_file "$issue")"
116	            [[ ! -f "$f" ]] && return 0
117	            local timeout; timeout="$(_ccgl_flock_timeout_sec)"
118	            (
119	                exec 9>"${f}.lock"
120	                flock -w "$timeout" 9 || exit 1
121	                grep -Fxv "$label" "$f" > "${f}.new" || true
122	                mv "${f}.new" "$f"
123	            )
124	            ;;
125	        *) return 1 ;;
126	    esac
127	}
128	
129	# _ccgl_read_holder <issue> — who the newest run-status comment names as holder.
130	_ccgl_read_holder() {
131	    local issue="$1" holder=""
132	    _ccgl_gh_lib || return 0
133	    case "${ZBUILD_CLAIM_BACKEND:-gh}" in
134	        local-fs)
135	            local rsc="${ZBUILD_CLAIM_STORE:-}/$issue/run-status-comment.txt"
136	            [[ -f "$rsc" ]] || return 0
137	            rsc_holder_line_v holder "$(cat "$rsc")"
138	            printf '%s' "$holder"
139	            ;;
140	        gh)
141	            _ccgl_slug || return 0
142	            rsc_holder_find "${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}" "$_CCGL_SLUG" "$issue"
143	            ;;
144	    esac
145	}
146	
147	_ccgl_refused() {
148	    local issue="$1" holder
149	    holder="$(_ccgl_read_holder "$issue" || true)"
150	    jq -nc --arg h "$holder" '{acquired: false, holder: $h}'
151	    printf 'claim-coordinator: issue #%s carries the %s label: another run is working on it. If that run is gone, remove the label: gh issue edit %s --remove-label %s\n' \
152	        "$issue" "$_CCGL_LABEL" "$issue" "$_CCGL_LABEL" >&2 || true
153	}
154	
155	# ─── Hook: claim <issue_id> ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
156	# stdout: {"acquired": true} | {"acquired": false, "holder": "<holder>"}
157	#         | {"acquired": false, "skipped": "<why>"} (no claim was attempted)
158	# rc: 0 answered, 1 backend error, 2 usage error.
159	claim_coordinator_claim() {
160	    local issue="$1"
161	    [[ -z "$issue" ]] && { printf 'claim_coordinator_claim: missing issue id\n' >&2 || true; return 2; }
162	    # The label is on GitHub (local-fs stands in for it): a run told to stay off
163	    # GitHub makes no claim there.
164	    if [[ "${NO_GITHUB:-}" == "true" ]]; then
165	        printf '{"acquired": false, "skipped": "NO_GITHUB=true"}\n'
166	        return 0
167	    fi
168	
169	    if ! _ccgl_read_labels "$issue"; then
170	        printf '{"acquired": false, "reason": "backend_read_error"}\n'
171	        return 1
172	    fi
173	    local line
174	    while IFS= read -r line; do
175	        [[ "$line" == "$_CCGL_LABEL" ]] && { _ccgl_refused "$issue"; return 0; }
176	    done <<< "$_CCGL_OUT"
177	
178	    # No hostname in the label: a laptop run and a CI run claim the same one.
179	    local add_rc=0
180	    _ccgl_add_label "$issue" "$_CCGL_LABEL" || add_rc=$?
181	    if [[ "$add_rc" -eq 2 ]]; then
182	        _ccgl_refused "$issue"
183	        return 0
184	    fi
185	    if [[ "$add_rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
186	        printf '{"acquired": false, "reason": "backend_error"}\n'
187	        return 1
188	    fi
189	    printf '{"acquired": true}\n'
190	    return 0
191	}
192	
193	# ─── Hook: release <issue_id> ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
194	claim_coordinator_release() {
195	    local issue="$1"
196	    [[ -z "$issue" ]] && { printf 'claim_coordinator_release: missing issue id\n' >&2 || true; return 2; }
197	    _ccgl_remove_label "$issue" "$_CCGL_LABEL" && return 0
198	    printf 'claim-coordinator: could not remove %s from issue #%s — remove the %s label by hand, or the next run of the issue is refused.\n' \
199	        "$_CCGL_LABEL" "$issue" "$_CCGL_LABEL" >&2 || true
200	    return 1
201	}
202	
203	# ─── Hook: heartbeat <issue_id> ───────────────────────────────────────────────
204	# Labels do not expire (a stale claim is #2533's).
205	claim_coordinator_heartbeat() {
206	    return 0
207	}
208	
209	# ─── Hook: takeover <issue> <holder> <by> <stale_s> <state_dir> ───────────────
210	# ADR-005 §3 (#2616): a claim another machine holds, judged on GitHub's clock
211	# and taken over when stale (lib/takeover.sh, loaded only here): released, and
212	# claimed again for this run. stdout: {"taken_over":true,"claimed":true,"age_s":N}
213	# | {"taken_over":false[,"failed":"<why>"]}.
214	claim_coordinator_takeover() {
215	    if ! declare -F claim_takeover_run >/dev/null 2>&1; then
216	        local _lrc=0
217	        # shellcheck source=lib/takeover.sh
218	        source "$_CCGL_DIR/lib/takeover.sh" 2>/dev/null || _lrc=$?
219	        if (( _lrc != 0 )) || ! declare -F claim_takeover_run >/dev/null 2>&1; then
220	            printf 'zbuild_claim_acquire: takeover.sh could not be loaded (%s) — refusing to take over %s\n' "$_CCGL_DIR/lib/takeover.sh" "${2:-}" >&2
221	            printf '{"taken_over":false}\n'; return 0
222	        fi
223	    fi
224	    claim_takeover_run "$1" "$2" "$3" "$4" "$5" claim_coordinator_release claim_coordinator_claim
225	}
226	
227	# ─── Hook: list_claims ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
228	# stdout: JSON array of {issue, holder, acquired_at}. rc 1 on a backend error.
229	claim_coordinator_list_claims() {
230	    case "${ZBUILD_CLAIM_BACKEND:-gh}" in
231	        gh)
232	            { _ccgl_slug && _ccgl_gh issue list --label "$_CCGL_LABEL" --json number --repo "$_CCGL_SLUG"; } || {
233	                printf 'list_claims: gh issue list failed\n' >&2 || true
234	                return 1
235	            }
236	            jq -c 'map({issue: .number, holder: "unknown", acquired_at: null})' <<< "$_CCGL_OUT" 2>/dev/null \
237	                || printf '[]\n'
238	            ;;
239	        local-fs)
240	            local store="${ZBUILD_CLAIM_STORE:?}"
241	            local results='[]' issue_dir issue holder
242	            for issue_dir in "$store"/*/; do
243	                [[ -f "$issue_dir/labels.txt" ]] || continue
244	                grep -Fxq "$_CCGL_LABEL" "$issue_dir/labels.txt" 2>/dev/null || continue
245	                issue="${issue_dir%/}"; issue="${issue##*/}"
246	                holder="$(_ccgl_read_holder "$issue" || true)"
247	                results="$(jq -c --arg i "$issue" --arg h "$holder" \
248	                    '. + [{issue: ($i|tonumber), holder: $h, acquired_at: null}]' <<< "$results")"
249	            done
250	            printf '%s\n' "$results"
251	            ;;
252	        *) printf '[]\n' ;;
253	    esac
254	    return 0
255	}

170	# Globals (not local) so EXIT trap can read them after main() returns.
171	_runner_run_id="" _runner_issue="" _runner_ended=false _runner_state_file=""
172	# ADR-054 §11 (#1944): run-level watchdog globals — PID of the watchdog background
173	# subshell (killed by the EXIT trap on clean exit) and the resolved limit in seconds.
174	_RUNNER_WATCHDOG_PID=""
175	_RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""

177	# reported once rather than once per stage boundary.

180	# ─── _runner_leaf_contract_halt <state_file> <stage> <reason> ───────────────
181	# A leaf stage whose v2 result the engine rejected ends the run; rc 0 when it
182	# did. A cycle already halts on this (#550); a leaf recorded `error` and went on,
183	# which is how #1835's run shipped a plan result with no `reason`. Safe ahead of
184	# #1798: a contract violation is a zBuild defect (ADR-054 §6 `broken`), never a
185	# transient failure, so this cannot turn a network hiccup into a dead run.
186	# Reads main()'s _runner_run_id / _runner_issue and sets its _runner_ended.
187	_runner_leaf_contract_halt() {
188	    local sf="$1" st="$2" why="${3:-}"
189	    [[ "$why" == contract_violation:* ]] || return 1
190	    _update_stage_status "$sf" "$st" "failed"
191	    _set_pipeline_status "$sf" "failed"
192	    eb_emit_event "stage.fail" "stage=$st" "reason=$why" 2>/dev/null || true
193	    eb_emit_event "pipeline.end" "status=failed" "stage=$st" "reason=$why" \
194	        "run_id=${_runner_run_id:-}" "issue=${_runner_issue:-}" 2>/dev/null || true
195	    _RUNNER_END_REASON="$why"   # #2607: the end-of-run words say this stop
196	    _render_pipeline_end "failed" "$st"
197	    _runner_ended=true
198	    error "Stage $st wrote a result the engine rejects ($why) — a zBuild defect; the run stops here"
199	    return 0
200	}

202	# _runner_stage_stop_word_v: scripts/lib/stage-stop-word.sh (#2611: the loop uses it too).
203	
204	# ─── _runner_leaf_verdict_halt <state_file> <stage> <class> <raw> ────────────
205	# #1798 (ADR-054 §4): a leaf stage that reports a failure ends the run; rc 0
206	# when it did. <class> is the classified verdict the runner already read
207	# (runner_read_stage_verdict: fail, or a structural word passed through);
208	# <raw> is the stage's own word, which the run's end names. A cycle acts on its
209	# members' verdicts; a leaf used to record one, pick a glyph from it and
210	# complete anyway. A template opts a stage out with `blocking: false`
211	# (ADR-013) — advisory by declaration, never by accident.
212	_runner_leaf_verdict_halt() {
213	    local sf="$1" st="$2" v="${3:-}" raw="${4:-}"
214	    case "$v" in
215	        fail|error|block|scope_violation|corrupt_diff) ;;
216	        *) return 1 ;;
217	    esac
218	    [[ "$(template_stage_blocking "$st" 2>/dev/null)" == "false" ]] && return 1
219	    [[ -n "$raw" && "$raw" != "missing" ]] || raw="$v"
220	    _update_stage_status "$sf" "$st" "failed"
221	    _zbuild_state_set_stage_verdict "$sf" "$st" "$v"
222	    _set_pipeline_status "$sf" "failed"
223	    # No `rc=` field: the stage exited 0, so a verdict-triggered stage.fail
224	    # carries the stage's word (`verdict=`) instead — as the contract halt
225	    # carries `reason=` alone. A consumer of stage.fail reads either shape.
226	    eb_emit_event "stage.fail" "stage=$st" "verdict=$raw" "reason=stage_failed:$raw" 2>/dev/null || true
227	    eb_emit_event "pipeline.end" "status=failed" "stage=$st" "reason=stage_failed:$raw" \
228	        "run_id=${_runner_run_id:-}" "issue=${_runner_issue:-}" 2>/dev/null || true
229	    _RUNNER_END_REASON="stage_failed:$raw"   # #2607: the end-of-run words say this stop
230	    _render_pipeline_end "failed" "$st"
231	    _runner_ended=true
232	    error "Stage $st reported $raw — the run stops here"
233	    return 0
234	}

237	# Report a failed stage-end push once per distinct reason, on the same channel
238	# and dedupe as a failed snapshot.
239	_runner_note_push_failure() {
240	    [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" == "failed" ]] || return 0
241	    [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-}" != "${_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON:-}" ]] || return 0
242	    _RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
243	    eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.failed" "stage=${1:-unknown}" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
244	        "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
245	    warn "stage-end push failed at stage '${1:-unknown}': ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"

248	# ─── _runner_push_work_branch <state_dir> <stage> (#2187) ────────────────────
249	# When the run has a work branch on origin (ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH — CI sets
250	# zbuild/issue-N-ci), push the run's commits to it at every stage end, so a new
251	# session can pick them up even if this runner dies. No changes, no save: only
252	# when HEAD carries commits past the commit the run started from, which the
253	# engine sets before any stage (#2367; #1801 run 38290215955: the end of hydrate
254	# force-pushed main over the branch's earlier work). Advisory: a failure is
255	# reported, never fatal.
256	_runner_push_work_branch() {
257	    local _branch="${ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH:-}"
258	    [[ -n "$_branch" ]] || return 0
259	    local _repo="${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}"
260	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || _repo="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
261	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || return 0
262	    git -C "$_repo" remote get-url origin >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
263	    local _base="${ZBUILD_RUN_START_COMMIT:-}" _ahead
264	    [[ -n "$_base" ]] || return 0
265	    _ahead="$(git -C "$_repo" rev-list --count "$_base..HEAD" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
266	    [[ "$_ahead" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_ahead" -gt 0 ]] || return 0
267	    local _err
268	    if _err="$(git -C "$_repo" push --force -q origin "HEAD:refs/heads/$_branch" 2>&1)"; then
269	        return 0
270	    fi
271	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
272	    # #2588: GitHub's words kept, the engine's tokens masked (as the state push).
273	    local _wb_why=""; _artifact_persist_push_reason_v _wb_why <(printf '%s\n' "$_err")
274	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="git push work branch $_branch failed: ${_wb_why:-<no stderr>}"
275	    _runner_note_push_failure "${2:-unknown}"
276	    return 0
277	}

279	# ─── _runner_keep_head_on_branch <state_dir> <stage> (#2264) ─────────────────
280	# A model call can leave HEAD off the run branch; every later commit then lands
281	# on HEAD alone while the branch ref — which pr-open checks out and the post-run
282	# step pushes — falls behind. #1844 run 37066147994 lost its work that way. At
283	# every stage end, put HEAD back on the branch when that drops nothing, and say
284	# which stage left it off; when the two diverged, move nothing and say so.
285	_runner_keep_head_on_branch() {
286	    local _stage="${2:-unknown}" _branch="${ZBUILD_RUN_BRANCH:-}"
287	    [[ -n "$_branch" ]] || return 0
288	    local _repo="${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}"
289	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || _repo="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
290	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || return 0
291	    zbuild_keep_head_on_branch "$_repo" "$_branch"
292	    case "$ZBUILD_HEAD_OUTCOME" in
293	        reattached)
294	            eb_emit_event "pipeline.head.reattached" "stage=$_stage" "branch=$_branch" \
295	                "was=$ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS" 2>/dev/null || true
296	            warn "stage '$_stage' left HEAD off the run branch ($ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS) — moved '$_branch' to HEAD" ;;
297	        diverged)
298	            eb_emit_event "pipeline.head.diverged" "stage=$_stage" "branch=$_branch" \
299	                "was=$ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS" 2>/dev/null || true
300	            warn "stage '$_stage' left HEAD off the run branch and the two diverged — '$_branch' not moved" ;;
301	    esac
302	    return 0
303	}

305	# ─── _runner_snapshot_artifacts <state_dir> <stage> (ADR-050, #1581/#1878) ───
306	# Snapshot the artifact area onto the state branch at a stage boundary, so a
307	# completed stage's work survives a mid-run crash/rate-limit and is available to
308	# the next run. Stage-agnostic (snapshots whatever files exist) and advisory —
309	# never blocks a run.
310	#
311	# #1878: ONE definition, called from every stage-completion site on the LIVE
312	# dispatch-unit path. It previously existed only inline in the legacy linear stage
313	# loop below — which no shipped template ever reaches (any cycle/map/parallel unit
314	# sets _run_dispatch_units=1, and every terminal branch of that block returns), so
315	# the snapshot was never invoked at all and the store was always empty. That is
316	# item 1 of #1807.
317	#
318	# #1878: also no longer swallows stderr. A snapshot that fails now says so, with
319	# the failing git operation named, instead of returning 1 into a `2>/dev/null`
320	# and leaving no trace anywhere.
321	_runner_snapshot_artifacts() {
322	    # $1 may be empty: the cycle-orchestrator call site is several frames from
323	    # main(), and relying on main()'s `state_dir` local reaching it through
324	    # dynamic scope is exactly the kind of implicit coupling that makes a call
325	    # site silently no-op. The runner exports the resolved per-run value at
326	    # runner.sh:1739, so fall back to that.
327	    local _snap_state_dir="${1:-}" _snap_stage="${2:-unknown}"
328	    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || _snap_state_dir="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
329	    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || return 0
330	    # Before the identity guard: a --goal or local run needs its branch kept too.
331	    _runner_keep_head_on_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
332	    # #1931: identity, not issue number. `issue > 0` excluded every --goal run
333	    # from the durable store, so nothing was ever snapshotted for one and the
334	    # push had nothing to send.
335	    _artifact_persist_has_identity "$_runner_issue" || return 0
336	
337	    _artifact_persist_snapshot "$_snap_state_dir" "$_runner_issue" || true
338	    case "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" in
339	        saved)
340	            eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.saved" \
341	                "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
342	                "skipped=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SKIPPED:-0}" 2>/dev/null || true
343	            ;;
344	        failed)
345	            # Loud, not fatal. This event is the whole point of #1878: the defect
346	            # went undiagnosed for the life of the feature because the failure had
347	            # no channel to surface on.
348	            #
349	            # Deduped on the reason. Most failures are a STATIC precondition — no
350	            # resolvable repository, a ref D/F conflict — so they recur identically
351	            # at every stage boundary. Reporting the first occurrence keeps the
352	            # signal; repeating it once per stage is noise that trains an operator
353	            # to ignore the event. A CHANGED reason is always reported.
354	            if [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-}" != "${_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON:-}" ]]; then
355	                _RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
356	                eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.failed" \
357	                    "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
358	                    "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
359	                warn "artifact snapshot failed at stage '$_snap_stage': ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
360	            fi
361	            ;;
362	        # empty / unchanged are not failures and are not events: emitting
363	        # `saved` for them is precisely the lie this change removes.
364	        *) : ;;
365	    esac
366	    # #2187: push at the stage end, not only when the run ends — a run killed
367	    # mid-way (job ceiling, SIGKILL) otherwise loses everything since its start.
368	    # Only for a run that declares where its work goes (ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH;
369	    # the CI pipeline sets it). A plain local run — and every test — pushes
370	    # nothing here: tests have left state branches in real checkouts, and
371	    # this would put them on origin. The persist stage still pushes at the end.
372	    [[ -n "${ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH:-}" ]] || return 0
373	    local _leak=""
374	    if _leak="$(_artifact_persist_find_secret "$_snap_state_dir/artifacts")"; then
375	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
376	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="refusing to push — artifact looks like it carries a credential (${_leak})"
377	        _runner_note_push_failure "$_snap_stage"
378	        # The scan covers the artifact area, not the working tree: the run's
379	        # code commits still go to the work branch.
380	        _runner_push_work_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
381	        return 0
382	    fi
383	    if [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" == "saved" ]]; then
384	        _artifact_persist_push "$_runner_issue" "${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}" || true
385	        _runner_note_push_failure "$_snap_stage"
386	    fi
387	    _runner_push_work_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
388	    return 0
389	}

405	# Millisecond wall clock. Honors ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE so goldens
406	# can pin the timestamp (same env var as stage-io.sh — single test contract;

408	# treated as unset (defensive: a stray export shouldn't crash the runner).
409	# Empty stdout on failure → caller renders "??:??:?? UTC" / "?s" — no crash.

417	        local us="${EPOCHREALTIME/./}"

419	        return 0

424	# ─── _runner_status_comment_spawn <state_dir> <events_jsonl> <repo_root> ─────
425	# #2131 (ADR-064): the live run-status comment is a SIDECAR that tails
426	# events.jsonl — the engine never renders GitHub markdown itself, it only
427	# starts an observer and stops it. Spawned here, in the runner, so a local
428	# `zbuild pipeline start --issue N` and the CI workflow share one code path
429	# (CI needs no extra step: GITHUB_TOKEN is already job-level env). Every
430	# gate that keeps a test's temp repo off GitHub lives in rsc_enabled; the
431	# harness also pins ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT=0. The sidecar's fd 3 is closed so
432	# it never holds the stage-io channel open.
433	_RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
434	_runner_status_comment_spawn() {
435	    local state_dir="$1" events_jsonl="$2" repo_root="${3:-$PWD}"
436	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
437	    # The explicit kill switch leaves NO trace — not even a log line. The
438	    # parity golden lists every file in the state dir, and every test runs
439	    # with the switch on (run-tests.sh); a "disabled" file there would be
440	    # noise in every fixture for a fact the operator already knows.
441	    [[ "${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT:-1}" == "0" ]] && return 0
442	    local lib="$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh"
443	    [[ -f "$lib" ]] || return 0
444	    # shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh
445	    source "$lib" 2>/dev/null || return 0
446	    rsc_enabled "$state_dir" "$repo_root" || return 0
447	    local slug; slug="$(zbuild_repo_slug "$repo_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
448	    ( exec 3>&- 2>/dev/null
449	      exec bash "$lib" --events "$events_jsonl" --state-dir "$state_dir" \
450	           --parent-pid $$ --slug "$slug" --issue "${ZBUILD_ISSUE:-0}" \
451	           --run-id "${ZBUILD_RUN_ID:-}" --repo-root "$repo_root" ) \
452	        </dev/null >>"$state_dir/status-comment.log" 2>&1 &
453	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=$!
454	    return 0
455	}

457	# ─── _runner_early_exit_trap ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
458	# ADR-005 §1: the exit trap from the claim until main() sets its own — it frees
459	# what the run holds by then (the claim, the issue lock, the run-cap slot).
460	_runner_early_exit_trap() {
461	    trap '' INT TERM
462	    zbuild_claim_release
463	    zbuild_issue_lock_release || true
464	    zbuild_run_cap_release || true

467	# ─── _runner_status_comment_reap ─────────────────────────────────────────────
468	# Idempotent (clears the pid first) and rc-neutral (`return 0`, every line
469	# tolerant): it runs inside the EXIT trap under `set -e`, and the process exit
470	# status must never depend on GitHub. TERM, bounded wait, KILL backstop.
471	_runner_status_comment_reap() {
472	    local pid="${_RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID:-}"
473	    [[ -n "$pid" ]] || return 0
474	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
475	    if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
476	        kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
477	        local i
478	        for (( i = 0; i < ${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_REAP_TIMEOUT:-45} * 10; i++ )); do
479	            kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break
480	            sleep 0.1
481	        done
482	        kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
483	    fi
484	    wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
485	    return 0
486	}

488	# ─── _runner_now_short (#508) — HH:MM:SS UTC for stage banners ───────────────
489	# Returns ??:??:?? UTC when the underlying clock primitive yields nothing
490	# (defensive — the operator-visible banner still renders without crashing).
491	_runner_now_short() {
492	    local ms; ms="$(_runner_now_ms)"
493	    if [[ -z "$ms" || ! "$ms" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
494	        printf '??:??:?? UTC'
495	        return 0
496	    fi
497	    local sec=$(( ms / 1000 ))
498	    local out

502	        || date -u -d "@$sec" +'%H:%M:%S UTC' 2>/dev/null \

507	# ─── _runner_duration_token <stage> (#508) ───────────────────────────────────
508	# Format the elapsed duration since the start cache was populated. Mirrors
509	# stage-io.sh::_stage_io_render_duration's "<N.N>s" for sub-minute durations;
510	# for >= 60 s we use "<m>m<ss>s" so a slow stage doesn't render as "127.4s".
511	# Cache miss → "?s" (no crash).
512	_runner_duration_token() {
513	    local stage="$1"
514	    local start="${_RUNNER_STAGE_START_MS[$stage]:-}"
515	    if [[ -z "$start" || ! "$start" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
516	        printf '?s'
517	        return 0
518	    fi
519	    local now; now="$(_runner_now_ms)"
520	    if [[ -z "$now" || ! "$now" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
521	        printf '?s'
522	        return 0
523	    fi
524	    local ms=$(( now - start ))
525	    (( ms < 0 )) && ms=0
526	    if (( ms < 60000 )); then
527	        awk -v m="$ms" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1fs", m/1000}'
528	    else
529	        local total_s=$(( ms / 1000 ))
530	        local mins=$(( total_s / 60 ))
531	        local secs=$(( total_s % 60 ))
532	        printf '%dm%02ds' "$mins" "$secs"

534	}

536	# ─── _runner_record_report <state_dir> <stage> <report-json> (#2189) ─────────
537	# Merge one dispatch's report into the run's record, artifacts/stage-reports.json
538	# (under artifacts/ so it is snapshotted and restored with the run): wiring
539	# files are unioned; owned files are kept per reporting stage, so the
540	# deny list can exempt the owner. Engine setup reads THIS record — never a
541	# stage's artifact by name. Best-effort: a failed merge leaves the prior record.
542	# Parallel members record concurrently, so the read-merge-write holds a mkdir
543	# lock (portable; flock is absent on stock macOS) — else a sibling's merge is lost.
544	# A lock left by a killed holder is reclaimed after 10s.
545	_runner_record_report() {
546	    local state_dir="$1" stage="$2" report="${3:-}"
547	    [[ -n "$state_dir" && -n "$stage" && -n "$report" && "$report" != "{}" ]] || return 0
548	    # Most stages report none of the setup fields — skip the lock and the jq fork.
549	    [[ "$report" == *'"owned_files"'* || "$report" == *'"wiring_files"'* ]] || return 0
550	    local rec="$state_dir/artifacts/stage-reports.json"
551	    local lock="$state_dir/.stage-reports.lock" _tries=0
552	    [[ -d "$state_dir/artifacts" ]] || mkdir -p "$state_dir/artifacts" 2>/dev/null || return 0
553	    # #2565: a lock held 10s was broken as a dead holder's, and a slow live one
554	    # (twelve parallel writers on a busy runner) lost a report. flock is freed
555	    # by the kernel when its holder dies, so it is never broken by hand.
556	    if declare -F zbuild_has_flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && zbuild_has_flock; then
557	        ( flock 9 || exit 0; _runner_report_merge "$rec" "$stage" "$report" ) \
558	            9>"$state_dir/.stage-reports.flock" 2>/dev/null || true
559	        return 0
560	    fi
561	    # Without flock: the lock records its holder and is broken only when that
562	    # holder is gone.
563	    local _held
564	    until mkdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; do
565	        if (( ++_tries > ${_ZB_REPORT_LOCK_TRIES:-200} )); then
566	            _runner_report_lock_stale_v _held "$lock" && _runner_report_lock_break "$lock" "$_held"
567	            _tries=0
568	        fi
569	        sleep 0.05
570	    done
571	    printf '%s' "$BASHPID" > "$lock/pid" 2>/dev/null || true
572	    _runner_report_merge "$rec" "$stage" "$report"
573	    # Released only while it is still ours: a lock broken under a holder (2
574	    # minutes) may be another writer's by now.
575	    local _mine=""; IFS= read -r _mine 2>/dev/null < "$lock/pid" || true
576	    [[ "$_mine" == "$BASHPID" ]] && { rm -f "$lock/pid"; rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; }
577	    return 0
578	}

580	# _runner_report_merge <record> <stage> <report> — the report merged into the
581	# record; called under the record's lock.
582	_runner_report_merge() {
583	    local rec="$1" tmp="$1.tmp.$BASHPID"
584	    [[ -s "$rec" ]] || printf '{}' > "$rec"
585	    if jq --arg s "$2" --argjson r "$3" '
586	            .wiring_files = ((.wiring_files // []) + ($r.wiring_files // []) | unique)
587	          | if ($r.owned_files // null) != null
588	              then .owned_files = ((.owned_files // {}) + {($s): ($r.owned_files | unique)})
589	              else . end' "$rec" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
590	        mv -f "$tmp" "$rec"
591	    else
592	        rm -f "$tmp"
593	    fi
594	    return 0
595	}

597	# _runner_report_lock_stale_v <var> <lock_dir> — rc 0 when the lock's holder is
598	# gone, its recorded pid (or "" when it has none) into <var>. A holder is gone
599	# when its pid is not running, or when the lock is older than any merge takes
600	# (2 minutes): a pid can be reused, and a lock between its mkdir and its pid
601	# write has none.
602	_runner_report_lock_stale_v() {
603	    local -n _rls="$1"; _rls=""
604	    IFS= read -r _rls 2>/dev/null < "$2/pid" || true
605	    if [[ "$_rls" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && kill -0 "$_rls" 2>/dev/null; then
606	        [[ -n "$(find "$2" -maxdepth 0 -mmin +2 2>/dev/null)" ]] && return 0
607	        return 1
608	    fi
609	    [[ "$_rls" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && return 0
610	    [[ -n "$(find "$2" -maxdepth 0 -mmin +2 2>/dev/null)" ]]
611	}

613	# _runner_report_lock_break <lock_dir> <pid judged gone> — moved aside first, so
614	# two waiters cannot both break it; put back when another holder took it since.
615	_runner_report_lock_break() {
616	    local _dead="$1.dead.$BASHPID" _now=""
617	    mv "$1" "$_dead" 2>/dev/null || return 0
618	    IFS= read -r _now 2>/dev/null < "$_dead/pid" || true
619	    # Put back only where nothing stands: mv onto a new lock would move it inside.
620	    if [[ "$_now" != "$2" ]]; then [[ -e "$1" ]] || mv "$_dead" "$1" 2>/dev/null || true; return 0; fi
621	    rm -rf "$_dead" 2>/dev/null
622	    return 0
623	}

625	# ─── _runner_validate_leaf_resolvability <stages_arr_name> <plugins_root> ─────
626	# ADR-047 §5: the manifest-derived membership fence — the sole membership
627	# enforcement (the old hardcoded-roster fence is deleted, #1299). Every leaf in the
628	# resolved template flow must resolve to a plugin via resolve_stage_plugin
629	# (role-then-id, ADR-042); an unresolved leaf names the id.
630	#
631	# It is a CONTRACT check, so it is gated by the SAME ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR mode
632	# the inter-stage contract-validator uses (they must agree). Load-time membership
633	# enforcement is the ENFORCE-mode job; the opt-out modes (warn/off) skip it — so
634	# this preflight is a TRUE NO-OP whenever enforcement is off and never perturbs the
635	# mock-roster suites that drive runner.sh under warn (they resolve their leaves at
636	# dispatch via mocked plugin_hook_call, not through a real registry):
637	#   - enforce (default, real runs) / unset → ERROR fail-closed (rc=2). This is the
638	#     load-time guarantee that replaces the old canonical membership gate.
639	#   - warn / off (or any unknown mode)     → skip. Dispatch-time resolution
640	#     (resolve_stage_plugin in the stage loop) still fails a genuinely-missing
641	#     plugin mid-run — the backstop for opt-out runs.
642	# Takes the stage array BY NAME to avoid a subshell copy on read.
643	_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability() {
644	    local _arr_name="$1" plugins_root="$2"
645	    # Only enforce gates at load; warn/off/unknown are opt-outs → no-op. (The
646	    # default is enforce, matching contract-validator's default; unknown modes
647	    # degrade to non-enforce, exactly as contract-validator degrades them to warn.)
648	    [[ "${ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR:-enforce}" == "enforce" ]] || return 0
649	    # Validate the array name is a plain identifier before binding the nameref
650	    # below — never bind a name assembled from unvalidated input (Copilot #1290:
651	    # injection footgun). Callers pass a literal ("active_stages"), so a
652	    # non-identifier is a programming error, not runtime data.
653	    if [[ ! "$_arr_name" =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ ]]; then
654	        error "_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: invalid array name '${_arr_name}'"
655	        return 1
656	    fi
657	    # bash errors on a nameref that resolves to itself; reject it with our own
658	    # message rather than a raw "circular name reference" from the shell.
659	    if [[ "$_arr_name" == "_stages" ]]; then
660	        error "_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: array name '_stages' collides with the nameref"
661	        return 1
662	    fi
663	    # Warm the manifest cache in THIS shell before resolving anything. Every
664	    # resolution below reads manifests through `$( )`, and an associative-array
665	    # write inside a command substitution dies with that subshell — so a lazily
666	    # filled cache is never inherited (#1614, the reason yaml_cache_prewarm
667	    # exists and main() calls it at line ~1370).
668	    #
669	    # main() is not the only entry point. Tests source this file and call helpers
670	    # directly, never reaching that prewarm, and then every lookup forks awk:
671	    # template-resolvability-preflight-test.sh made 28,068 yaml_get calls with
672	    # ZERO cache hits, at real 150s / user 52s / sys 81s — kernel time 1.55x
673	    # user, which is process creation, not computation. Prewarming here took it
674	    # to 82.75s with sys 81s -> 45s.
675	    #
676	    # Here and not in setup_test_env: the prewarm costs 1.32s, and 570 test
677	    # files would pay ~747s for it to benefit the few that resolve plugins.
678	    # Measured before choosing the seam.
679	    #
680	    # Idempotent: a second call re-reads the same keys, which are now cache
681	    # hits. Cheap no-op in production, where main() has already warmed it.
682	    if declare -F yaml_cache_prewarm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
683	        yaml_cache_prewarm "$plugins_root"
684	    fi
685	    # Discovery too, for the same reason and in the same shell: it validates
686	    # every manifest on every call (~1.47s even with the yaml cache warm) and
687	    # runs once per leaf. 19 leaves x 2 templates was 38 full re-validations of
688	    # an unchanged tree.
689	    if declare -F discover_plugins >/dev/null 2>&1; then
690	        discover_plugins "$plugins_root" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
691	    fi
692	    local -n _stages="${_arr_name}"
693	    local _leaf _ok=1
694	    for _leaf in "${_stages[@]+"${_stages[@]}"}"; do
695	        [[ -z "$_leaf" ]] && continue
696	        # A cycle/parallel GROUP id is a composition operator, not a leaf, and is
697	        # not itself a plugin — its members are already flattened into the stage
698	        # list. Skip group ids (their _TPL_STAGE_TYPE_<id> is cycle|parallel).
699	        local _t_var="_TPL_STAGE_TYPE_${_leaf//-/_}"
700	        case "${!_t_var:-leaf}" in
701	            cycle|parallel) continue ;;
702	        esac
703	        if ! resolve_stage_plugin "$_leaf" "$plugins_root" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
704	            error "load_template: stage '${_leaf}' resolves to no plugin (ADR-047 §5: every leaf must resolve via role or id; add a plugin whose provides.role matches, or whose id is '${_leaf}')"
705	            _ok=0
706	        fi
707	    done
708	    [[ $_ok -eq 1 ]]
709	}

711	# ─── _runner_validate_startup_preflight [violation_fixture] (ADR-051 §warn-first) ──
712	# Aggregation SKELETON (#1318 / D1): owns the violations[]/fail_count collection,
713	# the render-all-at-once block (same pattern as _contract_validate_pipeline) and the
714	# warn/enforce/off mode dispatch. Separate gate from _runner_validate_leaf_
715	# resolvability — it covers non-contract elements the DAG validator does not address.

718	# downstream, each against the discriminating fixtures #1605 pre-stages:
719	#   - persona-binding existence (PERSONA_MISSING) → #1320 (D3)
720	#   - requires.plugins resolution (PLUGIN_MISSING) → #1321 (D4)
721	# An earlier draft carried both checks here, untested; the requires.plugins one was
722	# an acknowledged approximation that raised spurious PLUGIN_MISSING for any entry
723	# naming an ordinary plugin. Shipping checks no test discriminates is the green-but-
724	# inert shape #1605 exists to prevent, so they were removed rather than carried.

726	# Deliberate divergence from _runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: the DEFAULT mode
727	# here is WARN (not enforce). This lands warn-first so operators see failures before
728	# enforcement is mandatory. Set ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=enforce to fail-closed.
729	# ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=off is a full no-op (skips all checks, emits nothing).
730	#
731	# The optional first argument is a synthetic violation fixture: it injects one
732	# pre-formed violation so the aggregation, rendering and mode dispatch are testable
733	# before any real producer exists. A non-empty string yields exactly one violation;
734	# empty (or omitted) yields none. Runtime call sites in runner.sh pass no argument,
735	# so until D3/D4 land the live path always renders nothing and returns 0.
736	# _runner_template_personas <template> — every persona the template names, one
737	# "<where>|<persona id>" per line: <where> is the section, or section/element
738	# for a map element's own persona (ADR-051 §2).
739	_runner_template_personas() {
740	    awk '
741	        function indent(s,   i) { i = 0; while (substr(s, i+1, 1) == " ") i++; return i }
742	        /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
743	        /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*:/ { sec = $0; sub(/:.*/, "", sec); el = ""; els_ind = -1; next }
744	        /^[[:space:]]+elements:[[:space:]]*$/ { els_ind = indent($0); next }
745	        els_ind >= 0 && /[^[:space:]]/ && indent($0) <= els_ind { els_ind = -1; el = "" }
746	        els_ind >= 0 && /^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]/ {
747	            el = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]+/, "", el); sub(/^id:[[:space:]]*/, "", el)
748	            sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, "", el); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, "", el); next
749	        }
750	        /^[[:space:]]+persona:[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]#]/ {
751	            id = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]+persona:[[:space:]]*/, "", id); sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, "", id)
752	            gsub(/[[:space:]"\047]/, "", id)
753	            print (el != "" ? sec "/" el : sec) "|" id
754	        }
755	    ' "$1" 2>/dev/null
756	}

914	    else
915	        local total_s=$(( ms / 1000 ))
916	        local mins=$(( total_s / 60 ))
917	        local secs=$(( total_s % 60 ))
918	        printf '%dm%02ds' "$mins" "$secs"

922	# ─── _pipeline_status_glyph <status> (#525) ──────────────────────────────────
923	# Thin shim mapping the ADR-006 pipeline status enum to a verdict class glyph
924	# (delegates to verdict_glyph from core/pipeline/verdict.sh, #507). The
925	# pipeline status enum is distinct from plugin verdicts on purpose — this is
926	# a render-only mapping for the terminal banner, NOT an extension of the
927	# verdict table itself.
928	#
929	# Mapping:
930	#   complete (banner-only; persisted event payload still says "success")
931	#                                          → pass  → ✓
932	#   failed | interrupted | aborted         → fail  → ✗
933	#   preflight_failed                       → warn  → ⚠
934	#   anything else                          → ⚠ (defensive)
935	_pipeline_status_glyph() {
936	    local status="${1:-}"
937	    case "$status" in
938	        complete|success)                        verdict_glyph "pass" ;;
939	        complete_unconverged)                    verdict_glyph "warn" ;;
940	        failed|interrupted|aborted|timed_out)    verdict_glyph "fail" ;;
941	        preflight_failed)                        verdict_glyph "warn" ;;
942	        *)                                       printf '%s' "?" ;;
943	    esac
944	}

946	# ─── _pipeline_status_color <status> (#525) ──────────────────────────────────
947	# Companion to _pipeline_status_glyph; delegates to verdict_color so NO_COLOR
948	# behavior matches the per-stage indicator line exactly.
949	_pipeline_status_color() {
950	    local status="${1:-}"
951	    case "$status" in
952	        complete|success)                        verdict_color "pass" ;;
953	        complete_unconverged)                    verdict_color "warn" ;;
954	        failed|interrupted|aborted|timed_out)    verdict_color "fail" ;;
955	        preflight_failed)                        verdict_color "warn" ;;
956	        *)                                       printf '%s' "${YELLOW:-}" ;;
957	    esac
958	}
959	
960	# ─── _render_pipeline_end <status> [stage] [rc] (#525) ───────────────────────
961	# Emits the terminal banner that closes a pipeline run, framed with ═ (U+2550)
962	# to distinguish the pipeline boundary from the stage divider (━) and stage-io
963	# banners (─). Two-line layout:
964	#
965	#   ════════════════ pipeline.end ════════════════ HH:MM:SS UTC
966	#   <glyph> Pipeline <status_word>: status=<X> run_id=<Y> issue=<N> (took <dur>)
967	#
968	# Frame bars colored BLUE (chrome). Glyph + leading status word inherit the
969	# verdict class color (foreground signal). Right-aligned timestamp via the
970	# same width math as _render_stage_divider — degrades to a symmetric divider
971	# (no timestamp) when mid_bar <= 2.
972	#
973	# Writes to fd 2 so it composes correctly with other operator lines (info /
974	# success / error) under the same output redirection rules. Banner is emitted
975	# AFTER the pipeline.end JSONL event so the durable event is fail-closed
976	# against banner-write failures.
977	# _runner_restore_stderr — point fd 2 back at the runner's own stderr, saved at
978	# startup in _RUNNER_ERR_FD (ADR-054 §7). A trap that fires inside a call made
979	# with 2>/dev/null runs under that redirect, so the abort banner went to
980	# /dev/null when SIGTERM landed during one. A no-op when nothing was saved.
981	_runner_restore_stderr() {
982	    # Guard against a repeat signal (e.g. `timeout` forwarding its own SIGTERM
983	    # to the process group after the first already fired). Called only from
984	    # _runner_abort_trap (EXIT trap). Setting the guard here — as the very first
985	    # instruction inside the function body — closes the race window that exists
986	    # AFTER this function returns to _runner_abort_trap: bash checks pending
987	    # signals at function-return boundaries, so a pending second TERM would fire
988	    # _runner_signal_trap TERM (→ exit 1) before the explicit guard in
989	    # _runner_abort_trap could execute. By setting it HERE the guard is already
990	    # active by the time the function returns. B3 is satisfied because
991	    # _runner_restore_stderr is still the first call in _runner_abort_trap.
992	    # Ignored, not trapped with ':' (#2493): a handler run inside the trap broke
993	    # it off on bash 5.2, and a TERM to the group ended the trap's own command
994	    # substitutions, which take the default TERM.
995	    trap '' INT TERM
996	    [[ -n "${_RUNNER_ERR_FD:-}" ]] && exec 2>&"$_RUNNER_ERR_FD"
997	    return 0
998	}
999	
1000	_render_pipeline_end() {
1001	    local status="${1:-unknown}"
1002	    local stage_hint="${2:-}"
1003	    local rc_hint="${3:-}"
1004	    local run_id="${_runner_run_id:-?}"
1005	    local issue="${_runner_issue:-?}"
1006	    # Best-effort value gathering. Each `$(...)` here forks a helper that may
1007	    # itself fork an external (awk in the duration token, date/tput in the
1008	    # clock/width helpers). Most call sites invoke this banner DIRECTLY under the
1009	    # runner's `set -e` (e.g. the cycle/stage abort + LLM/scope-abort paths) —
1010	    # not wrapped in `|| true` — so a transient under-load fork failure in any
1011	    # one of these bare assignments would trip errexit and abort the render
1012	    # BEFORE the printf block, silently dropping the operator's terminal banner
1013	    # mid-teardown. `|| fallback` neutralizes errexit at each assignment so the
1014	    # banner is always emitted once the function is reached, on every call site.
1015	    # (#1156)
1016	    local dur; dur="$(_runner_pipeline_duration_token)" || dur='?s'
1017	    local glyph; glyph="$(_pipeline_status_glyph "$status")" || glyph='✗'
1018	    local color; color="$(_pipeline_status_color "$status")" || color=''
1019	    local frame="${BLUE:-}"
1020	    local ts; ts="$(_runner_now_short)" || ts='??:??:?? UTC'
1021	    local width; width="$(_term_width)" || width=80
1022	
1023	    # Map status → operator-friendly verb for line 2. Tracks event payload
1024	    # verbatim so "status=<X>" agrees with the verb. ("success" in legacy
1025	    # event payloads renders as "complete" — see ADR-015 §v5 amendment).
1026	    local word
1027	    case "$status" in
1028	        success|complete)        word="complete" ;;
1029	        complete_unconverged)    word="complete_unconverged" ;;
1030	        failed)                  word="failed" ;;
1031	        interrupted)             word="interrupted" ;;
1032	        aborted)                 word="aborted" ;;
1033	        timed_out)               word="timed_out" ;;
1034	        preflight_failed)        word="preflight_failed" ;;
1035	        *)                       word="$status" ;;
1036	    esac
1037	
1038	    local label=" pipeline.end "
1039	    # Layout: <left_bar><label><mid_bar> <ts>
1040	    local left_bar=$(( (width - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1) / 2 ))
1041	    local mid_bar=$(( width - left_bar - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1 ))
1042	
1043	    local detail_status="status=${status}"
1044	    [[ -n "$stage_hint" ]] && detail_status+=" stage=${stage_hint}"
1045	    [[ -n "$rc_hint"    ]] && detail_status+=" rc=${rc_hint}"
1046	
1047	    if [[ "$mid_bar" -le 2 ]]; then
1048	        # Degraded layout — drop timestamp from the header.
1049	        local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1050	        [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1051	        local bar
1052	        printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1053	        bar="${bar// /═}"
1054	        {
1055	            printf '\n'
1056	            printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' "$frame" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" "$frame" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1057	            printf '%b%b%s%b Pipeline %s: %s run_id=%s issue=%s (took %s)\n' \
1058	                "$color" "${BOLD:-}" "$glyph" "${RESET:-}" \
1059	                "$word" "$detail_status" "$run_id" "$issue" "$dur"
1060	        } >&2
1061	        _runner_render_open_items "$status" || true
1062	        return 0
1063	    fi
1064	
1065	    local lbar rbar
1066	    printf -v lbar '%*s' "$left_bar" ''; lbar="${lbar// /═}"
1067	    printf -v rbar '%*s' "$mid_bar"  ''; rbar="${rbar// /═}"
1068	    {
1069	        printf '\n'
1070	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b %s\n' \
1071	            "$frame" "$lbar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1072	            "$frame" "$rbar" "${RESET:-}" "$ts"
1073	        printf '%b%b%s%b Pipeline %s: %s run_id=%s issue=%s (took %s)\n' \
1074	            "$color" "${BOLD:-}" "$glyph" "${RESET:-}" \
1075	            "$word" "$detail_status" "$run_id" "$issue" "$dur"
1076	    } >&2
1077	    _runner_render_open_items "$status" || true
1078	}
1079	
1080	# _runner_render_open_items <status> — #2330 (ADR-068 §8): a run that did not
1081	# pass ends by saying why in words and naming each open item, with what would
1082	# settle it. pipeline.end keeps the engine's code; this is what a reader sees.
1083	_runner_render_open_items() {
1084	    case "${1:-}" in failed|interrupted|aborted|timed_out) ;; *) return 0 ;; esac
1085	    [[ -n "${_runner_state_file:-}" ]] && declare -F open_items_markdown >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
1086	    local sd="${_runner_state_file%/*}" items n reason="${_RUNNER_END_REASON:-${_CYCLE_LAST_TERMINATED_REASON:-}}"
1087	    # The watchdog fires outside any cycle, so the status is the reason (#1944).
1088	    [[ "$1" == timed_out ]] && reason=timed_out
1089	    items="$(open_items_markdown "$sd")" || items=""
1090	    n=0; [[ -n "$items" ]] && n="$(grep -c '^[0-9][0-9]*\. ' <<< "$items" || true)"
1091	    {
1092	        printf 'The run %s.\n' "$(run_end_words "$reason" "$n")"
1093	        [[ -n "$items" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$items"
1094	        # #2508: and the questions design could not settle.
1095	        local q; q="$(open_items_questions "$sd")" || q=""
1096	        [[ -n "$q" ]] && printf '\n%s\n' "$q"
1097	    } >&2
1098	}
1099	
1100	# ─── _render_stage_divider <stage> (#492, ts: #508) ──────────────────────────
1101	# Emits a blank line + a heavy horizontal rule (━ U+2501) with the stage name
1102	# centered in stage-color, then another blank line — written to fd 2 so it
1103	# survives the same redirection rules as ▸/✓/✗ info lines. Used on every
1104	# stage transition (between eb_emit_event "stage.start" and "▸ Running stage")
1105	# so the operator's eye finds the next stage boundary at a glance.
1106	#
1107	# #508: right-align an HH:MM:SS UTC timestamp on the divider, mirroring the
1108	# stage-io banner header right-alignment (_stage_io_compose_banner). Width
1109	# math (no bookend glyphs in this layout — just bars + label + sep + ts):
1110	#   visible = left_bar + len(label) + mid_bar + 1 (space) + len(ts)
1111	#   left_bar = (width - len(label) - len(ts) - 1) / 2
1112	#   mid_bar  = width - left_bar - len(label) - len(ts) - 1
1113	# Degrade rule: when mid_bar <= 2 (very narrow terminals) we drop the
1114	# timestamp and emit the legacy symmetric divider so layout stays legible.
1115	_render_stage_divider() {
1116	    local stage="$1"
1117	    local width
1118	    width="$(_term_width)"
1119	    local color
1120	    color="$(_stage_color "$stage")"
1121	    local label=" ${stage} "
1122	    local ts; ts="$(_runner_now_short)"
1123	
1124	    # Layout: <left_bar><label><mid_bar> <ts>
1125	    # Visible width = left_bar + len(label) + mid_bar + 1 (sep) + len(ts).
1126	    local left_bar=$(( (width - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1) / 2 ))
1127	    local mid_bar=$(( width - left_bar - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1 ))
1128	
1129	    if [[ "$mid_bar" -le 2 ]]; then
1130	        # Degraded: legacy symmetric divider, no timestamp (narrow terminal).
1131	        local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1132	        [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1133	        local bar
1134	        printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1135	        bar="${bar// /━}"
1136	        {
1137	            printf '\n'
1138	            printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' "$color" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" "$color" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1139	            printf '\n'
1140	            # #523: trailing blank line — combined with the existing leading
1141	            # \n above, produces two stacked blanks between consecutive stages.
1142	            # Cycle sub-dividers (ADR-015 §v6) intentionally do NOT add this.
1143	            printf '\n'
1144	        } >&2
1145	        return 0
1146	    fi
1147	
1148	    local lbar rbar
1149	    printf -v lbar '%*s' "$left_bar" ''; lbar="${lbar// /━}"
1150	    printf -v rbar '%*s' "$mid_bar"  ''; rbar="${rbar// /━}"
1151	    {
1152	        printf '\n'
1153	        # %b on colored fragments so \033[...] resolves like echo -e elsewhere.
1154	        # Timestamp is plain text outside color escapes — NO_COLOR keeps it.
1155	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b %s\n' \
1156	            "$color" "$lbar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1157	            "$color" "$rbar" "${RESET:-}" "$ts"
1158	        printf '\n'
1159	        # #523: trailing blank line — combined with the leading \n above,
1160	        # produces two stacked blanks between consecutive stages. Cycle
1161	        # sub-dividers (ADR-015 §v6) intentionally do NOT add this.
1162	        printf '\n'
1163	    } >&2
1164	}
1165	
1166	# ─── Cycle banner helpers (#524, ADR-015 §v6, ADR-021) ───────────────────────
1167	# Operator-fd-2 chrome for outer cycles (ADR-021). These render a visual
1168	# hierarchy that nests cleanly with the existing stage-transition divider
1169	# (_render_stage_divider) so the operator can see cycle entry, per-iter
1170	# boundaries, per-iter outcomes, and cycle exit in the scrollback.
1171	#
1172	# Glyph + color ladder (heaviest → lightest):
1173	#   ━━━ (U+2501) stage transition   — BOLD BLUE (handled in _render_stage_divider)

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# E2E: claimants racing for one issue on the github-labels coordinator's local-fs
3	# store (ADR-005 §2). The store's add is checked and made under one lock, so it
4	# has a single winner; GitHub's label add has no such check, which is #2534's.
5	#
6	# R1 a 4-way race: no backend error, every reply is valid JSON
7	# R2 …exactly one claimant has acquired=true; the others acquired=false
8	# R3 …and the issue carries zbuild:claimed exactly once
9	# R4 the winner's release removes it
10	# R5 list_claims lists a claimed issue
11	set -euo pipefail
12	
13	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
14	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
15	
16	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
17	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
18	# shellcheck source=../lib/test-helpers.sh
19	source "$REPO_ROOT/tests/lib/test-helpers.sh"
20	
21	print_test_header "claim-coordinator race (ADR-005)"
22	setup_test_env "claim-race"
23	skip_unless_capable "flock unavailable — the local-fs claim store needs it" command -v flock
24	
25	PLUGIN_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels"
26	export ZBUILD_CLAIM_BACKEND="local-fs"
27	export ZBUILD_CLAIM_STORE="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/claim-store"
28	unset NO_GITHUB
29	
30	# shellcheck source=../../core/plugin-registry/registry.sh
31	source "$REPO_ROOT/core/plugin-registry/registry.sh"
32	set +e; validate_manifest "$PLUGIN_DIR/manifest.yaml" >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?; set -e
33	assert_eq "github-labels manifest validates as claim-coordinator" "0" "$rc"
34	
35	ISSUE=90001841 N=4 OUT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/race"
36	mkdir -p "$OUT"
37	pids=()
38	for i in $(seq 1 "$N"); do
39	    (
40	        # shellcheck source=../../plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh
41	        source "$PLUGIN_DIR/plugin.sh"
42	        rc=0; claim_coordinator_claim "$ISSUE" > "$OUT/$i.json" 2> "$OUT/$i.err" || rc=$?
43	        echo "$rc" > "$OUT/$i.rc"
44	    ) &
45	    pids+=("$!")
46	done
47	for p in "${pids[@]}"; do wait "$p" || true; done
48	
49	winners=0 losers=0 bad=0
50	for i in $(seq 1 "$N"); do
51	    if [[ "$(cat "$OUT/$i.rc")" != "0" ]]; then bad=$((bad + 1)); continue; fi
52	    case "$(jq -r '.acquired' "$OUT/$i.json" 2>/dev/null || echo unparsed)" in
53	        true) winners=$((winners + 1)) ;;
54	        false) losers=$((losers + 1)) ;;
55	        *) bad=$((bad + 1)) ;;
56	    esac
57	done
58	assert_eq "[R1] no backend error or unreadable reply" "0" "$bad"
59	assert_eq "[R2] exactly one winner" "1" "$winners"
60	assert_eq "[R2] …the other $((N - 1)) are refused" "$((N - 1))" "$losers"
61	LABELS="$ZBUILD_CLAIM_STORE/$ISSUE/labels.txt"
62	assert_eq "[R3] the issue carries zbuild:claimed exactly once" "1" "$(/usr/bin/grep -cx 'zbuild:claimed' "$LABELS" || true)"
63	
64	# shellcheck source=../../plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh
65	source "$PLUGIN_DIR/plugin.sh"
66	assert_eq "[R5] list_claims lists the claimed issue" "1" \
67	    "$(claim_coordinator_list_claims | jq --argjson i "$ISSUE" 'map(select(.issue == $i)) | length')"
68	claim_coordinator_release "$ISSUE"
69	assert_eq "[R4] release removes zbuild:claimed" "0" "$(/usr/bin/grep -cx 'zbuild:claimed' "$LABELS" || true)"
70	
71	cleanup_test_env
72	print_test_results
73	exit $((FAIL > 0))

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# E2E: claimants racing for one issue on the github-labels coordinator's local-fs
3	# store (ADR-005 §2). The store's add is checked and made under one lock, so it
4	# has a single winner; GitHub's label add has no such check, which is #2534's.
5	#
6	# R1 a 4-way race: no backend error, every reply is valid JSON
7	# R2 …exactly one claimant has acquired=true; the others acquired=false
8	# R3 …and the issue carries zbuild:claimed exactly once
9	# R4 the winner's release removes it
10	# R5 list_claims lists a claimed issue
11	set -euo pipefail
12	
13	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
14	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
15	
16	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
17	source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
18	# shellcheck source=../lib/test-helpers.sh
19	source "$REPO_ROOT/tests/lib/test-helpers.sh"
20	
21	print_test_header "claim-coordinator race (ADR-005)"
22	setup_test_env "claim-race"
23	skip_unless_capable "flock unavailable — the local-fs claim store needs it" command -v flock
24	
25	PLUGIN_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels"
26	export ZBUILD_CLAIM_BACKEND="local-fs"
27	export ZBUILD_CLAIM_STORE="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/claim-store"
28	unset NO_GITHUB
29	
30	# shellcheck source=../../core/plugin-registry/registry.sh
31	source "$REPO_ROOT/core/plugin-registry/registry.sh"
32	set +e; validate_manifest "$PLUGIN_DIR/manifest.yaml" >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?; set -e
33	assert_eq "github-labels manifest validates as claim-coordinator" "0" "$rc"
34	
35	ISSUE=90001841 N=4 OUT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/race"
36	mkdir -p "$OUT"
37	pids=()
38	for i in $(seq 1 "$N"); do
39	    (
40	        # shellcheck source=../../plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh
41	        source "$PLUGIN_DIR/plugin.sh"
42	        rc=0; claim_coordinator_claim "$ISSUE" > "$OUT/$i.json" 2> "$OUT/$i.err" || rc=$?
43	        echo "$rc" > "$OUT/$i.rc"
44	    ) &
45	    pids+=("$!")
46	done
47	for p in "${pids[@]}"; do wait "$p" || true; done
48	
49	winners=0 losers=0 bad=0
50	for i in $(seq 1 "$N"); do
51	    if [[ "$(cat "$OUT/$i.rc")" != "0" ]]; then bad=$((bad + 1)); continue; fi
52	    case "$(jq -r '.acquired' "$OUT/$i.json" 2>/dev/null || echo unparsed)" in
53	        true) winners=$((winners + 1)) ;;
54	        false) losers=$((losers + 1)) ;;
55	        *) bad=$((bad + 1)) ;;
56	    esac
57	done

59	assert_eq "[R2] exactly one winner" "1" "$winners"
60	assert_eq "[R2] …the other $((N - 1)) are refused" "$((N - 1))" "$losers"
61	LABELS="$ZBUILD_CLAIM_STORE/$ISSUE/labels.txt"
62	assert_eq "[R3] the issue carries zbuild:claimed exactly once" "1" "$(/usr/bin/grep -cx 'zbuild:claimed' "$LABELS" || true)"

65	source "$PLUGIN_DIR/plugin.sh"

67	    "$(claim_coordinator_list_claims | jq --argjson i "$ISSUE" 'map(select(.issue == $i)) | length')"

69	assert_eq "[R4] release removes zbuild:claimed" "0" "$(/usr/bin/grep -cx 'zbuild:claimed' "$LABELS" || true)"

1	# Design: Concurrent-claim race detection (issue #2534)
2	
3	## Decision
4	
5	GitHub's label API has no check-and-set: two runs can both read "no claim" and both add
6	`zbuild:claimed`, each getting a success reply. After adding the label (gh backend only),
7	the coordinator posts a concurrent claim note — `"concurrent claim by \`<holder>\`"` —
8	then re-reads the GitHub issue itself (its labels or state), then reads back all trusted
9	concurrent claim notes. The note is the synchronous holder record (RQTIE-3 path 1). The
10	run whose note is first by GitHub's `created_at` (then `id` on a tie) is the winner; it
11	returns `{"acquired": true}`. Every other run marks its note "not started — concurrent
12	claim: `<winner>` was first" and returns
13	`{"acquired": false, "holder": "<winner>", "race_lost": true}`. The engine receives
14	`race_lost: true` and refuses immediately, skipping the stale-takeover path that would
15	otherwise trigger for any cross-machine refusal. ADR-005 gains §5 to document all of this.
16	
17	Why the stale-takeover path cannot set `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED` for a race-lost response:
18	in `zbuild_claim_acquire`, the new `race_lost: true` branch (DSRACE-5) returns 1 before
19	the code reaches `_zbuild_claim_takeover`, so the takeover's `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED="$issue"`
20	assignment is never reached. DSRACE-4 is [code] because that guarantee requires DSRACE-5 to
21	be in place; without it, the existing takeover path can and does set `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED`.
22	
23	Reviewed alternatives: GitHub's `labeled` events are not usable as the tie-break — GitHub
24	does not create a second `labeled` event when the label is already there, so the events
25	give no information about concurrent adders. The local-fs test backend is unaffected; its
26	`flock`-serialised add already returns rc 2 for a duplicate add.
27	
28	Outside assumptions:
29	- `rsc_gh` and `jq` are available in the coordinator (already used throughout `plugin.sh`)
30	- GitHub's comment `created_at` and `id` are ordered and stable (standard API guarantee)
31	- The concurrent claim note format (`"concurrent claim by \`"`) is distinct from takeover
32	  notes (`"took over a stale claim from \`"`) — no interference
33	
34	```steps
35	- 1 Add `_ccgl_self_holder_v`, `_ccgl_race_note_post_v`, `_ccgl_race_note_delete`, `_ccgl_race_note_update`, `_ccgl_race_note_first_v` to plugin.sh; extend `claim_coordinator_claim` to: post the concurrent claim note, re-read the GitHub issue, then read back concurrent claim notes, returning `race_lost: true` for the loser (gh backend only) | areas: plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh | serves: DSRACE-1, DSRACE-2, DSRACE-3, DSRACE-7
36	- 2 In `zbuild_claim_acquire`, detect `race_lost: true` in the refused reply and refuse immediately (skip stale-takeover, print concurrent-winner message) | areas: core/claim/claim.sh | serves: DSRACE-4, DSRACE-5
37	- 3 Amend ADR-005: add §5 (concurrent claim detection: arbitration note, first-by-created_at-then-id wins, loser updates note to not-started, `race_lost` skip); extend `Enforced by` | areas: docs/adr/ADR-005-claim-coordinator.md | serves: DSRACE-6
38	```
39	
40	```acceptance
41	DSRACE-1[code]: After successfully adding the zbuild:claimed label (gh backend), the claim posts a concurrent claim note with the run's holder, then reads back all trusted concurrent claim notes to detect concurrent claimants covers: RQTIE-1, RQTIE-3
42	  Given: the zbuild:claimed label was just successfully added via the gh backend
43	  When: the claim posts a "concurrent claim by `<holder>`" note and reads back all trusted concurrent claim notes since the note's own created_at minus the detection window
44	  Then: the note is posted synchronously before the read-back
45	  And: all concurrent claim notes from the current label epoch are returned
46	
47	DSRACE-2[code]: Only the run whose concurrent claim note is first (by created_at, then id) returns {"acquired": true}; all others return {"acquired": false} covers: RQTIE-2, RQTIE-1
48	  Given: two or more concurrent claim notes exist for the same issue within the detection window
49	  When: each run compares the notes and identifies the first
50	  Then: the run whose note has the earliest created_at returns {"acquired": true}
51	  And: all other runs return {"acquired": false, "holder": "<winner_holder>", "race_lost": true}
52	
53	DSRACE-3[code]: The losing run updates its concurrent claim note body to "not started" covers: RQCMT-1
54	  Given: the run's concurrent claim note is not the first by created_at (or id)
55	  When: the run determines it has lost the race
56	  Then: the run PATCHes its note body to "not started — concurrent claim: `<winner>` was first"
57	
58	DSRACE-4[code]: When zbuild_claim_acquire receives {"acquired": false, "race_lost": true} from the coordinator, _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED is not set and zbuild_claim_release does not remove the zbuild:claimed label covers: RQLBL-1
59	  Given: claim_coordinator_claim returns {"acquired": false, "race_lost": true}
60	  When: zbuild_claim_acquire processes the response
61	  Then: _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED is not set
62	  And: zbuild_claim_release does not remove the zbuild:claimed label
63	
64	DSRACE-5[code]: A coordinator response with race_lost: true causes zbuild_claim_acquire to refuse immediately without entering the stale-takeover path, printing a message that names the concurrent winner covers: RQTIE-1
65	  Given: claim_coordinator_claim returns {"acquired": false, "holder": "<winner>", "race_lost": true}
66	  When: zbuild_claim_acquire processes the response
67	  Then: the stale-takeover hook is not called
68	  And: stderr names the concurrent winner as the first claimant
69	
70	DSRACE-6[doc]: ADR-005 §5 tells a reader: after adding the label (gh backend), a note is posted as the holder record, the first note by created_at then id wins, the loser marks its note "not started", and race_lost: true in the refused response skips the stale-takeover path covers: RQADR-1
71	
72	DSRACE-7[code]: After posting the concurrent claim note (the synchronous holder record, gh backend), the claim reads back the GitHub issue's current state before proceeding with arbitration covers: RQREB-1
73	  Given: the zbuild:claimed label was added and the concurrent claim note was posted synchronously
74	  When: the claim reads the GitHub issue's current labels or state
75	  Then: fresh issue data is obtained from GitHub after the synchronous holder record was written
76	
77	WIRING: core/claim/claim.sh
78	```

1	# GitHub Labels Claim Coordinator
2	
3	**Plugin id:** `claim-coordinator-github-labels`
4	**Kind:** `claim-coordinator`
5	**ADR:** [ADR-005 — Claim Coordinator](../../../docs/adr/ADR-005-claim-coordinator.md)
6	
7	## Purpose
8	
9	The default cross-machine claim. The engine calls this plugin's `claim` hook before a run's first stage and its `release` hook on exit (ADR-005 §1). One shared GitHub issue label, `zbuild:claimed`, means "a run is working on this issue" — the same label for a laptop run and a CI run. Who holds it is not in the label: it is the `<!-- zbuild-holder: … -->` line of the holder's run-status comment (ADR-064), read back only from comments by the CI bot or by a repository owner, member or collaborator.
10	
11	## Contract (ADR-005)
12	
13	| Hook | Signature | stdout | Exit codes |
14	|---|---|---|---|
15	| `claim_coordinator_claim` | `claim <issue_id>` | `{"acquired": true}`, `{"acquired": false, "holder": "…"}`, or `{"acquired": false, "skipped": "…"}` | 0 answered, 1 backend error, 2 usage error |
16	| `claim_coordinator_release` | `release <issue_id>` | — | 0 removed, 1 failed (stderr says to remove the label by hand) |
17	| `claim_coordinator_heartbeat` | `heartbeat <issue_id>` | — | 0 always (labels don't expire; staleness is #2533) |
18	| `claim_coordinator_list_claims` | `list_claims` | `[{"issue": N, "holder": "...", "acquired_at": null}]` | 0 success, 1 backend error |
19	
20	## Behaviour
21	
22	- **Missing label.** A repository that does not define `zbuild:claimed` gets it (`gh label create --force`) the first time an add fails with "not found"; the add is then tried once more.
23	- **Every `gh` call is bounded** by the run-status comment's watchdog (`rsc_gh`, `ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_GH_TIMEOUT`): a hung `gh` cannot hold up a run's exit.
24	- **`NO_GITHUB=true`** makes no claim: the reply is `skipped`, and the engine records `pipeline.claim.skipped`.
25	- **Clearing a claim by hand.** Removing the `zbuild:claimed` label clears it. Until #2533, that is the only way to clear the claim of a run that crashed before its exit path — or of a cancelled GitHub Actions job: the cancel sends INT, then TERM, then KILL a few seconds later, and the KILL can land while the exit path is still running the always-run stages and persist, which come before the release.
26	- **The holder named on a refusal** is from the newest trusted run-status comment that names one. A finished run's comment names none, so the holder is a run still going, or one that died without finishing; a newer comment that names none (a refused run's) does not hide it. With no such comment (the holder posts none: `ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT=0`), the refusal says the holder is unknown.
27	
28	## Known limit: two runs claiming at the same moment
29	
30	GitHub's label add does not check whether the label is already there. Two runs that read "no label" at the same moment can both add it and both start. Nothing here prevents that; #2534 settles it.
31	
32	## Environment variables
33	
34	| Variable | Default | Description |
35	|---|---|---|
36	| `ZBUILD_CLAIM_BACKEND` | `gh` | `gh` (GitHub), or `local-fs` (a flock-serialised local store, for tests) |
37	| `ZBUILD_CLAIM_STORE` | _(required for local-fs)_ | Directory of the local-fs store: `<issue>/labels.txt`, and `<issue>/run-status-comment.txt` for the holder |
38	| `ZBUILD_CLAIM_FLOCK_TIMEOUT_SEC` | `5` | flock wait for the local-fs store |
39	| `ZBUILD_CLAIM_MACHINE_ID` | `${HOSTNAME}` | The machine named in a local run's holder (engine side, `core/claim/claim.sh`) |
40	| `ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_GH_TIMEOUT` | `30` | Seconds a `gh` call may take |
41	
42	The test harness (`setup_test_env`) sets `NO_GITHUB=true` and the local-fs store, so a test never claims on GitHub.
43

content.content:
# Design: Concurrent-claim race detection (issue #2534)

## Decision

GitHub's label API has no check-and-set: two runs can both read "no claim" and both add
`zbuild:claimed`, each getting a success reply. After adding the label (gh backend only),
the coordinator posts a concurrent claim note — `"concurrent claim by \`<holder>\`"` —
then re-reads the GitHub issue itself (its labels or state), then reads back all trusted
concurrent claim notes. The note is the synchronous holder record (RQTIE-3 path 1). The
run whose note is first by GitHub's `created_at` (then `id` on a tie) is the winner; it
returns `{"acquired": true}`. Every other run marks its note "not started — concurrent
claim: `<winner>` was first" and returns
`{"acquired": false, "holder": "<winner>", "race_lost": true}`. The engine receives
`race_lost: true` and refuses immediately, skipping the stale-takeover path that would
otherwise trigger for any cross-machine refusal. ADR-005 gains §5 to document all of this.

Why the stale-takeover path cannot set `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED` for a race-lost response:
in `zbuild_claim_acquire`, the new `race_lost: true` branch (DSRACE-5) returns 1 before
the code reaches `_zbuild_claim_takeover`, so the takeover's `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED="$issue"`
assignment is never reached. DSRACE-4 is [code] because that guarantee requires DSRACE-5 to
be in place; without it, the existing takeover path can and does set `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED`.

Reviewed alternatives: GitHub's `labeled` events are not usable as the tie-break — GitHub
does not create a second `labeled` event when the label is already there, so the events
give no information about concurrent adders. The local-fs test backend is unaffected; its
`flock`-serialised add already returns rc 2 for a duplicate add.

Outside assumptions:
- `rsc_gh` and `jq` are available in the coordinator (already used throughout `plugin.sh`)
- GitHub's comment `created_at` and `id` are ordered and stable (standard API guarantee)
- The concurrent claim note format (`"concurrent claim by \`"`) is distinct from takeover
  notes (`"took over a stale claim from \`"`) — no interference

```steps
- 1 Add `_ccgl_self_holder_v`, `_ccgl_race_note_post_v`, `_ccgl_race_note_delete`, `_ccgl_race_note_update`, `_ccgl_race_note_first_v` to plugin.sh; extend `claim_coordinator_claim` to: post the concurrent claim note, re-read the GitHub issue, then read back concurrent claim notes, returning `race_lost: true` for the loser (gh backend only) | areas: plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh | serves: DSRACE-1, DSRACE-2, DSRACE-3, DSRACE-7
- 2 In `zbuild_claim_acquire`, detect `race_lost: true` in the refused reply and refuse immediately (skip stale-takeover, print concurrent-winner message) | areas: core/claim/claim.sh | serves: DSRACE-4, DSRACE-5
- 3 Amend ADR-005: add §5 (concurrent claim detection: arbitration note, first-by-created_at-then-id wins, loser updates note to not-started, `race_lost` skip); extend `Enforced by` | areas: docs/adr/ADR-005-claim-coordinator.md | serves: DSRACE-6
```

```acceptance
DSRACE-1[code]: After successfully adding the zbuild:claimed label (gh backend), the claim posts a concurrent claim note with the run's holder, then reads back all trusted concurrent claim notes to detect concurrent claimants covers: RQTIE-1, RQTIE-3
  Given: the zbuild:claimed label was just successfully added via the gh backend
  When: the claim posts a "concurrent claim by `<holder>`" note and reads back all trusted concurrent claim notes since the note's own created_at minus the detection window
  Then: the note is posted synchronously before the read-back
  And: all concurrent claim notes from the current label epoch are returned

DSRACE-2[code]: Only the run whose concurrent claim note is first (by created_at, then id) returns {"acquired": true}; all others return {"acquired": false} covers: RQTIE-2, RQTIE-1
  Given: two or more concurrent claim notes exist for the same issue within the detection window
  When: each run compares the notes and identifies the first
  Then: the run whose note has the earliest created_at returns {"acquired": true}
  And: all other runs return {"acquired": false, "holder": "<winner_holder>", "race_lost": true}

DSRACE-3[code]: The losing run updates its concurrent claim note body to "not started" covers: RQCMT-1
  Given: the run's concurrent claim note is not the first by created_at (or id)
  When: the run determines it has lost the race
  Then: the run PATCHes its note body to "not started — concurrent claim: `<winner>` was first"

DSRACE-4[code]: When zbuild_claim_acquire receives {"acquired": false, "race_lost": true} from the coordinator, _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED is not set and zbuild_claim_release does not remove the zbuild:claimed label covers: RQLBL-1
  Given: claim_coordinator_claim returns {"acquired": false, "race_lost": true}
  When: zbuild_claim_acquire processes the response
  Then: _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED is not set
  And: zbuild_claim_release does not remove the zbuild:claimed label

DSRACE-5[code]: A coordinator response with race_lost: true causes zbuild_claim_acquire to refuse immediately without entering the stale-takeover path, printing a message that names the concurrent winner covers: RQTIE-1
  Given: claim_coordinator_claim returns {"acquired": false, "holder": "<winner>", "race_lost": true}
  When: zbuild_claim_acquire processes the response
  Then: the stale-takeover hook is not called
  And: stderr names the concurrent winner as the first claimant

DSRACE-6[doc]: ADR-005 §5 tells a reader: after adding the label (gh backend), a note is posted as the holder record, the first note by created_at then id wins, the loser marks its note "not started", and race_lost: true in the refused response skips the stale-takeover path covers: RQADR-1

DSRACE-7[code]: After posting the concurrent claim note (the synchronous holder record, gh backend), the claim reads back the GitHub issue's current state before proceeding with arbitration covers: RQREB-1
  Given: the zbuild:claimed label was added and the concurrent claim note was posted synchronously
  When: the claim reads the GitHub issue's current labels or state
  Then: fresh issue data is obtained from GitHub after the synchronous holder record was written

WIRING: core/claim/claim.sh
```
